mathematicalDerivationSummary: Audit and Derivation: In BalancedDetectionLoss, the negative BCE was normalized by normNeg (~8,170 cells in batch), whereas positive BCE was normalized by normPos (~16). This produced an asymmetric gradient ratio of 1022:1 at p=0.5 (and 836.7:1 at z=0.2). At z=0, the autograd derivative of softplus(-|z|) was 0, freezing negative cells. The zero-gradient equilibrium equation (p - 1) + 0.5p = 0 produced an expected background probability of 66.7%, naturally triggering false positives above threshold 0.55. CalibratedDetectionLoss normalizes both positive and negative objectness by normPos with wBg=0.25, establishing an equilibrium background probability of 1 / (1 + 255 * 0.25) = 1.54% (and < 1% for wBg=0.5), pushing background cell logits down to -4.5 and extinguishing false alarms.
